name: pfQuest xpGuide 2.1.0
body:
Everything since 2.0.2 (2.0.3 was not released on its own).

### Renamed: pfQuest-xpGuide
The addon folder is now **`pfQuest-xpGuide`**, named like pfQuest's other extensions (pfQuest-turtle).
- **Delete the old `pfQuest_xpGuide` folder** in `Interface\AddOns`. If both are there, the new one switches the old one off and tells you.
- **To keep your settings:** with the game closed, rename `WTF\Account\<account>\SavedVariables\pfQuest_xpGuide.lua` to `pfQuest-xpGuide.lua`. WoW names that file after the addon folder.
- **Installing from git:** clone into a folder named `pfQuest-xpGuide`.

### New: each guide begins with what it needs from the guides before
A guide whose quests need quests from an earlier guide begins with those steps. For example, Alah'Thalas' The Silver Covenant needs the Quel'Thalas Gate chain up to Message for the Windrunner. The steps have their places and the arrow on each. Done ones pass by themselves: handed in, or a later quest of their chain in your log. So the guide only asks for what is really missing. The prerequisites come from pfQuest's database (what the game requires), not optional lead-ins.

### Changed
- **Settings are per character.** Each character's first login copies the account's settings once. After that, what it changes stays its own.
- **pfQuest's markers by default.** pfQuest's map markers show, and pfQuest-turtle's sword and bag on nameplates, next to the mob's level. The guide's own markers (nameplate !, ?, skull and sack, and its map marker) come back with Settings -> Helpers -> **Use xpGuide's own markers**.
- **A guide started on a character that has played already starts where it is.** It goes by the quests recorded as handed in and your quest log. With nothing recorded, it also goes by your level. The chat says which step it starts at and why.
- **The High Elf and Goblin starting guides go in rounds, as RestedXP's guides do.** At each hub you hand in what's finished and pick up everything offered there and at the hubs close by. One step then does all the objectives, and you go back to hand them all in.
- **The High Elf guides are now 1-6 Quel'Thalas Gate and 6-11 Alah'Thalas.** The Gate guide gets you to level 6 before Veloren Brightstar (the Feltouched Letter), asks to move on at 6, and Alah'Thalas starts at 6. A place saved under the old names carries on.
- **The starting guides sit in their side's 1-20 folder, listed by level.** "1-6 Quel'Thalas Gate" and "6-11 Alah'Thalas" are in xpGuide Fast route Alliance 1-20, and "1-11 Blackstone Island" is in Horde 1-22, among RestedXP's starting zones.
- **"Take and hand in quests" takes only the step's quests.** It takes the next steps' quests only from the step's own NPC, never from a quest giver standing beside it.
- **pfQuest's arrow is the default** when your pfQuest has one and it is switched on; otherwise the guide's own arrow is used.
- **Moving on to the next guide keeps what that guide needs.** "Hand in, then move on" and "Move on now" both keep the quests the next guide depends on: picked up, done and handed in on the way, with the arrow on each. The High Elf start's Message for the Windrunner is one, so Vereesa now offers The Silver Covenant. "Move on now" skips your other finished hand-ins.

### New
- **A character's first start asks your server's experience rate (1x or 2x) and your professions** before the guide starts. Skip starts it with the settings as they are.
- **`/xpg moveon`** asks the move-on question at once, whatever your level, to try it.

### Fixed
- A quest started by an item a creature drops ("A Letter from the Royalty", from Veloren Brightstar) now points the arrow at that creature, not at a quest giver who doesn't offer it.
- The starting guides no longer hand out quests far above your level. Alah'Thalas gave level 8-10 quests at level 5, because it went by the lowest level the game offers them at. Now a quest comes when you are at most 1 level below it, with a "reach level" step first where needed. A quest from an item a creature drops waits until you are a level above the creature.
- A class trainer visit when a guide starts at an even level (6-11 Alah'Thalas at 6). A trainer that stands off the route (the High Elf Mage's) gets its own trip instead of none.
- A quest too hard for you no longer drops out of the guide when you walk away. "Take and hand in quests" leaves such a quest to you, and the step now waits with one line: take it anyway, or come back at the level it names (Skip step leaves it out).
- "Love, No Matter What" and "Kaelin's Gift" could be skipped when you came into the Alah'Thalas guide at level 4.
